<explanation>
Based on the provided file tree and README, I'll explain how to create a comprehensive system design diagram for MinIO, a high-performance object storage system. Here's how to approach the diagram:

1. Main Components (Core Architecture):

   a. API Layer
   - Draw an entry point showing S3-compatible API endpoints (port 9000)
   - Include Console UI interface (port 9001)
   - Show authentication/authorization components (found in cmd/auth-handler.go)

   b. Core Services Layer
   - Object Operations (cmd/object-handlers.go)
   - Bucket Operations (cmd/bucket-handlers.go)
   - IAM & Policy Management (internal/iam/)
   - Encryption Services (internal/crypto/)

   c. Storage Layer
   - Erasure Coding Implementation (cmd/erasure-*.go)
   - Drive Management (internal/disk/)
   - Data Format Handling (cmd/xl-storage*.go)

2. Key Subsystems (Draw as Connected Modules):

   a. Data Processing
   - Compression (docs/compression)
   - Encryption (internal/crypto)
   - S3 Select (internal/s3select)

   b. Management & Monitoring
   - Metrics System (cmd/metrics-v3*.go)
   - Logging System (internal/logger)
   - Health Checking (cmd/healthcheck-handler.go)

   c. Integration Components
   - Event Notification System (internal/event)
   - Lambda Functions (internal/config/lambda)
   - Replication System (cmd/bucket-replication*.go)

3. Cross-Cutting Concerns (Show as Vertical Layers):

   a. Security
   - TLS/SSL Handling
   - IAM & Authentication
   - Encryption at Rest

   b. High Availability
   - Distributed Locking (internal/dsync)
   - Replication Management
   - Health Monitoring

4. External Integrations (Show as External Systems):

   a. Storage Backends
   - Local Disk Storage
   - Optional Tiering to Cloud Storage

   b. Authentication Providers
   - LDAP
   - OpenID Connect
   - External IAM

5. Data Flow Indicators:

   - Use solid arrows for synchronous operations
   - Use dashed arrows for asynchronous operations
   - Use different colors for control flow vs data flow
   - Show primary data paths through the system

6. Deployment View (Include as Separate Section):

   - Single-Node Deployment
   - Distributed Deployment with Erasure Coding
   - Load Balancer Configuration
   - Console UI Access

7. Legend:

   - Color coding for different types of components
   - Line style definitions
   - Component type indicators
   - Security boundary markers

Specific Implementation Guidelines:

1. Use distinct shapes:
   - Rectangles for core services
   - Cylinders for storage components
   - Hexagons for security components
   - Clouds for external services

2. Color scheme:
   - Blue for core services
   - Green for storage components
   - Red for security elements
   - Gray for external integrations

3. Layer organization:
   - Top: Client-facing services
   - Middle: Core processing
   - Bottom: Storage and persistence

4. Include annotations for:
   - Port numbers
   - Protocol information
   - Scaling capabilities
   - Security boundaries

5. Add important details:
   - Minimum system requirements
   - Erasure coding configuration
   - Network ports and protocols
   - Security certificates and key management

This diagram should effectively communicate MinIO's architecture while maintaining readability and providing sufficient technical detail for implementation understanding.
